bottom_line: Over 6 weeks in the open-label STELLAR trial, rosuvastatin 10 to 40 mg reduced non-HDL-C by 42.0% to 50.9% compared with 34.4% to 48.1% with atorvastatin, 26.0% to 41.8% with simvastatin, and 18.6% to 27.4% with pravastatin.
implications: These 6-week data support that rosuvastatin 10–40 mg produced larger percentage reductions in non-HDL-C (42.0%–50.9%) and apo B (36.7%–45.3%) than the reported ranges for atorvastatin (34.4%–48.1%; 29.4%–42.9%), simvastatin (26.0%–41.8%; 22.2%–34.7%), and pravastatin (18.6%–27.4%; 14.7%–23.0%) in this trial; they do not, by themselves, establish effects on clinical outcomes, which the document notes are ongoing.

major_points.text: Pairwise comparisons were prospectively planned between rosuvastatin 10/20/40 mg and milligram-equivalent or higher doses of comparator statins with Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold P<0.002.
major_points.quote: pairwise comparisons were prospectively planned and performed between rosuvastatin 10, 20, and 40 mg and milligram-equivalent or higher doses of comparators.

major_points.text: A total of 2268 patients were randomized to the rosuvastatin 10- to 40-mg, atorvastatin, simvastatin, and pravastatin groups; mean age 57 (12) years; 51% women.
major_points.quote: A total of 2268 patients were randomized...Fifty-one percent of patients were women, the mean (SD) age was 57 (12) years

major_points.text: Rosuvastatin lowered non-HDL-C more than comparators across dose ranges, with reported percentage reductions for each statin.
major_points.quote: Rosuvastatin reduced non-HDL-C by 42.0% to 50.9% compared with 34.4% to 48.1% with atorvastatin, 26.0% to 41.8% with simva- statin, and 18.6% to 27.4% with pravastatin.

major_points.text: Rosuvastatin reduced apo B more than comparators across dose ranges, with reported percentage reductions for each statin.
major_points.quote: Rosuvastatin reduced apo B by 36.7% to 45.3% compared with 29.4% to 42.9% with atorvastatin, 22.2% to 34.7% with simvastatin, and 14.7% to 23.0% with pravastatin.

major_points.text: Among treatment completers, 94.4% completed the 6-week trial.
major_points.quote: Overall, 94.4% of patients (n = 2142) who were randomized to treatment completed the 6-week trial.
